messages:
sylvia: Customer request: per-tenant outbound allowlists + operator-managed SNAT pool for Private installs. They want policies that survive upgrades.
laura: Compliance-heavy. Do they expect agent enforcement or installer-level ACLs?
tim_r: Agent enforcement so rules travel with tenant manifests.
derek: That implies an RBAC model: tenant-admin vs platform-admin edits. Also migration guarantees for upgrades.
sylvia: Example: ‘Team A can only reach analytics.example.com and S3.’ Need both FQDN/CIDR allowlist + controlled egress IPs.
jen: Important: if we change enforcement backend (iptables -> eBPF -> cloud NAT) we must migrate without dropping sessions.
laura: Proposed: 1) EgressPolicy CRD (declarative), 2) enforcementVersion in CRD, 3) agent compatibility shim.
tim_r: CRD sketch:
```yaml
apiVersion: infra.redwood/v1
kind: EgressPolicy
metadata:
  tenant: acme
spec:
  allowedDestinations:
    - dns: analytics.example.com
    - cidr: 10.0.0.0/24
  egressMode: SNAT
  snatPool: tenant-acme-pool
  enforcementVersion: v1
```
derek: enforcementVersion lets us roll v2 (eBPF) safely. Agent must translate v1->v2 in compat mode.
jen: Console needs effective-policy view, dry-run, audit trail, and KMS-backed signing for operator overrides.
sylvia: Rollback semantics: use "compat translate" rather than deny-by-default to avoid outages.
laura: SNAT migration: preserve IPs for long sessions with ephemeral mapping window.
tim_r: eBPF preferred for scale but fallback to iptables for older kernels. Document kernel compatibility matrix.
derek: Acceptance criteria: CRD v1 + docs, agent enforcer (iptables + optional eBPF), migration shim tests, console view, RBAC + audit logs.
jen: Add customer acceptance: tenant-admin request path + SLA for enforcement time. KMS signing for tamper evidence in Private.
ops-bot: created INFR-5123: egress policy backlog https://redwood.internal/board/INFR-5123
sylvia: Action: laura+tim draft CRD & migration sketch by Thu EOD; derek+ops prototype iptables shim; jen mock console wireframe. I'll sync with AM for SLA wording.
laura: Will start draft.
jen: Wireframe tomorrow. :eyes:
